meanings.note: the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order
the comparative 'быстрее', often as an order

examples.text: Виталик, почему мы так медленно едем? Быстрее!
examples.trans: Vitalik, why are we going so slowly? Faster!

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have.

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.
Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?
All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people

meanings.en: other forms: вас (gen/acc), вам (dat), вами (instr), вас (prep)

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
+ dative of person + accusative of thing
imperative давай/давайте + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

related.gloss: to hand in; to take (an exam)

meanings.note: на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.

meanings.note: Used for women too. From Latin 'director' (one who guides or manages, from 'dirigere', to direct).

examples.trans: I want to talk to the director.

examples.text: Я один раз позвонила как директор и отменила контрольную.
examples.trans: Once I phoned pretending to be the headmistress and cancelled a test.

звонить.gloss: to call, to phone; to ring

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
Sorry, I didn't mean to offend you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, excuse me, there's someone here to see you.

meanings.note: Как вы знаете = as you know.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!
The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.
The oligarch will dine with us?

examples.text: Знаменитый олигарх будет сегодня ужинать в нашем ресторане?
examples.trans: Will the famous oligarch be dining at our restaurant tonight?

examples.text: Для стола олигарха заказали самую дорогую чёрную икру.
examples.trans: The most expensive black caviar was ordered for the oligarch's table.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

examples.text: Ладно, не буду тебя отвлекать сейчас.
examples.trans: All right, I won't distract you now.

examples.text: Луи, извини, что я отвлекаю тебя от работы.
examples.trans: Louis, sorry for distracting you from work.

examples.text: Купи себе платье или бабушке что-нибудь.
examples.trans: Buy yourself a dress or something for your grandmother.
She is wearing a pretty summer dress.

examples.text: Подожди. Купи себе платье или бабушке что-нибудь.
examples.trans: Wait. Buy yourself a dress or something for your grandmother.

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!

получаться.gloss: to work out, to come out

meanings.note: не получается = it isn't working, I can't (manage it)

examples.text: Нет, не получается у меня это забыть. Удачи тебе на новом месте работы.
examples.trans: No, I just can't forget it. Good luck to you in your new job.

meanings.note: from a trip, by car, train or plane

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

пройтись.gloss: to walk over, to go over; to take a stroll

meanings.en: to go over (a surface with a tool)
to take a stroll, to walk around

examples.trans: He even went over them with a pumice stone.
Let's take a stroll through the park.

meanings.note: Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.
We'll definitely have a big wedding!

examples.text: Макс, зачем ты соврал про нашу будущую свадьбу?
examples.trans: Max, why did you lie about our future wedding?
Then a wedding, and then kids!

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.
Why are you sitting in the corner?

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

examples.text: Они заняли свободный столик у окна.
examples.trans: They took a free table near the window.
Would you like to sit at an available table?
To a guest at the next table.

examples.text: Хорошо, тогда с тебя весёлый сценарий праздника.
examples.trans: Good, then you are responsible for a fun party script.
Go ahead and read your script.

examples.text: Я точно не помню его адрес.
examples.trans: I don't remember his exact address.

examples.text: Точно, полиция была! А что с машиной?
examples.trans: That's right, the police were there! And what about the car?

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
На приём он пришёл во фраке.
examples.trans: He came to the reception in a tailcoat.

examples.text: Какое хорошее утро! Лидия Алексеевна, чашку кофе, пожалуйста.
examples.trans: What a lovely morning! Lidia Alekseyevna, a cup of coffee, please.

examples.text: Подождите, у нас столик на четверых.
examples.trans: Wait, our table is for four.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: used with people and pluralia tantum: шестеро детей

examples.text: Вообще-то у этой актрисы шестеро детей.
examples.trans: Actually, that actress has six children.
And you end up with six people.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
